dedupe_keys.name: new orleans levee system 2005 failure modes and lessons learned from hurricane katrina asdso

description: This case study is the ASDSO account of how the New Orleans levee system performed in Hurricane Katrina in August 2005. The levees were built over more than 200 years by many owners, were described as a system in name only, and had gaps in the east and west bank lines; more than half the protected ground lies below sea level, by 10 to 12 feet in places, so all rain and interior drainage must be pumped out, and over 200 closure structures formed part of the line of defence. Katrina brought a surge and wave impact of 15 to 28 feet, estimated at a 50-year to 500-year event depending on location, and reversed the flow of the Mississippi. More than 50 breaches were documented, 46 due to overtopping, with over 1,800 lives lost and billions in damage. The page then summarises the consensus failure modes and the safety lessons and advances that followed, with tabs for photos, lessons learned and other resources. Coverage: one city and one event, narrative with figures. Access: free web page; licence not stated. Caveats: an encyclopaedic summary of other assessments, not primary data. It informs flood defence system reliability, overtopping and breach modelling and pumped-drainage scenarios, and relates to the ASDSO incident database and the Katrina hospital case studies in the catalogue.
